subject: general
question: Which Articles of the Constitution of India deals with the provision of Attorney General of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 76**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 76 of the Constitution of India, which deals with the provision of the Attorney General of India.
 
• Article 76 specifies the appointment, duties, and qualifications of the Attorney General of India, who is the highest law officer in the country.
 
• The Attorney General is appointed by the President of India and must be a person qualified to be a judge of the Supreme Court.
 
• The primary role of the Attorney General is to provide legal advice to the Government of India and represent it in legal matters before the Supreme Court and High Courts.
 
• The Attorney General has the right to speak and take part in proceedings of both Houses of Parliament but does not have the right to vote.
 
• The position of the Attorney General is not a full-time role, and they can engage in private legal practice, provided it does not conflict with their official duties.
 
• The Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President, meaning they can be removed at any time by the President.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Article 46, Article 66, and Article 56 do not pertain to the Attorney General; they deal with other provisions such as the promotion of educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and other weaker sections (Article 46), the election of the Vice-President of India (Article 66), and the term of office of the President of India (Article 56).
